> Preserved P059 planning source. Start with the [current build plan](README.md)
> for the selected Love Burn proposal. Dimensions, depicted equipment, LED
> allocations and delivery status below describe that earlier study; they are
> not current fabrication specifications or fresh supplier quotes.

# Material routes and alternate hosts

## Holder route M1 — Identified new steel

1. Complete the sphere/contact and load-path review before specifying stock.
2. Ask the fabricator for grade, tube/section, wall, joint and corrosion details
   on a controlled drawing, with an actual cut list and fabrication tolerances.
3. Quote stock, cut/roll work, plates, retained joints, consumables, finish and
   transport. The nominal triangle side is a layout length, not a saw setting.
4. Receive material with identification, inspect and measure it; reject defects
   under the fabricator's criteria.
5. Build a jig, fabricate and inspect under the accepted method; record mass and
   update the common-holder inventory. Dry-fit the ring and all contact padding.

## M2 — Known remnants / salvaged straight members

1. Inventory actual available pieces, lengths, sections, corrosion and provenance.
2. Reviewer/fabricator decides which pieces can be identified and accepted for
   each job; unknown steel is not automatically acceptable in the occupied load path.
3. Compare all-in cost including cleaning, inspection, new joints and rejected
   yield with M1. Do not book a savings until the usable stock is accepted.
4. Issue the cut list against identified pieces; segregate rejected/decorative stock.
5. Follow M1 fabrication/inspection, retaining piece-to-assembly traceability.

## M3 — Six-foot trampoline ring donor

1. Identify and measure the exact donor; “six foot” may describe outer size,
   not ring centreline. Record tube section, wall, segment/joint retention and condition.
2. Reviewer assesses the changed load direction, concentrated interfaces,
   corrosion and joints. The original trampoline's ground-use rating does not
   transfer to a sphere seat or lifting component.
3. Compare accepted donor refurbishment and retention costs with a rolled ring.
   Reject a donor when condition/material cannot be established.
4. Design the loop/triangle interfaces and padding against the selected sphere;
   the nominal CAD has 14.4 mm centreline overhang at side midpoints.
5. Fabricate only the accepted adaptation, inspect it and update the model and
   mass. M3 replaces the M1 rolled-ring item; it never creates a second ring purchase.

## Host H1 — Existing aerial rig (preferred candidate for suspension)

1. Identify actual rig and manual, ownership/loan permission and inspection history.
2. Measure usable attachment height, span and leg/spreader envelope in its intended configuration.
3. Obtain written confirmation/review for this occupied apparatus, total load,
   outdoor ground/wind and recovery arrangement; an aerial rating alone is not enough.
4. Follow S25/S30 only if those checks pass; otherwise retain ground mode.

## H2 — Purpose-designed freestanding gantry / tripod

1. Treat it as a different host with its own drawing and quote, not scrap added
   above the completed sphere.
2. Reviewer defines member/joint design, foundations/restraint, complete payload,
   lateral effects and recovery; preserve front access and full arm clearance.
3. Compare delivered, inspected and installed cost against H1 and ground mode.
4. Fabricate/obtain only the accepted host and its inspection/assembly records.
5. Re-run every S25/S30 host, unoccupied-test and operational gate. No detailed
   fabrication plan is released for an unidentified host.

## H3 — Lighting-truss goalpost / crank stands

1. Obtain the exact manufacturer/model and intended load/application documentation.
2. Confirm with manufacturer and qualified reviewer whether an occupied suspended
   apparatus and its loads are permitted. Lighting-equipment capacity is not
   permission to lift or support a person.
3. If not permitted, reject this host for occupancy; do not substitute a larger
   stated SWL as a workaround.
4. If applicable permission/design is obtained, document locking, lowering,
   stability, footing, redundancy and access, quote it and follow S25/S30 gates.

## H4 — Existing overhead point or tree (site-specific investigation)

1. Obtain explicit venue/property approval for the exact location and use; trees
   in a public park are not presumed available anchors.
2. For a structural point, obtain its documented support capacity and allowed
   load directions. For a tree, engage an appropriate arborist plus the rigging/
   structural reviewer; a photograph or trunk diameter does not supply a rating.
3. Reviewer defines non-damaging interfaces, load path, independent requirements,
   clearances, weather limits and rescue for the selected apparatus.
4. Quote all required services/hardware and accept or reject within budget.
5. Only an accepted site-specific system proceeds through S25/S30. Otherwise
   use the reviewed lander option. No tree-wrapping/branch-selection recipe is assumed.

Truck cantilevers, receiver/fifth-wheel mounts and wood platforms remain excluded
from active procurement. They are historical model references, not unfinished
steps in the current build.
